The Bureau of Land Management suggests a discussion of the new procedure which has been done in revision of the draft EIS. Comment from the Indiana Division of Nature Preserves under the Department of Natural Resources says, "More definite criteria needs to be formulated on how it will be determined when a species or subspecies is becoming endangered." The Executive Office of the Indiana Department of Natural Resources seems to fear that endangered species "likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction" may block development programs. Their comment: "If the Secretary of the Interior is given discretionary authority in the designation of species which may sometime in the future become endangered, the action of placing these species on the endangered species list could limit or place unreasonable restrictions on justifiable Federal and State land and water resource programs."
Another of several constructive comments from the <u>Washington</u> Game Department says, "A more definitive explanation of 'likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction' is needed. This phrase is extremely speculative and vague; judgments made on this criterion would lack credibility.

Also this phrase when tied to the words 'subspecies' and 'extinction' lacks the preciseness required in a scientific approach to this important problem."
Arizona, through the Department of Economic Planning and Development, says
